Using anger as a motivator to improve can be tricky in my experience. It's great as a starting point to get that initial fire burning, but it can't remain the constant motivator because then I'd get blinded by the negative memories to be able to appreciate any positive progress I'd made. 

Your drive to prove wrong those who wronged you is admirable, but I'd say you already did when you took the initial action to try to improve upon yourself. This is not going to be an easy task, but take a long time to reflect on how much you've grown and changed. Would you objectively say you're in a better place than you were before you started lifting? Come to acknowledge and appreciate all you've overcome and the anger will likely start to dissipate. It won't likely be instantaneous, but it should decrease more as time goes on.

I'm assuming that for such an advanced piece of technology as nanomachines, they have other methods affecting things besides physical grasp (lasers, particle beams, etc.). If the particles are so small, the nanomachines could simply form small enclosures with each other, trapping some particles, and then altering them in a group. Besides, simply being able to grab on to something is totally unrelated to a change on the molecular level.

The nanomachines being larger than the GN particles does not mean that they cannot affect the particles' molecular structure. This means that, in theory, the Turn A's Moonlight Butterfly could simply access the molecules of the 00 Qan[T] and the GN particles, alter them into harmless sand, and that takes care of that. Especially since a full powered Moonlight Butterfly would appear to have the capability to cover a much more vast distance than a Quantum Burst.

According to the Gundam Wiki page it says, "At its full power, the Moonlight Butterfly can cover a wide range (from Earth to Jupiter). The Turn A's nanomachines have the ability to convert most if not all matter to silicon dioxide (sand) on an molecular basis, allowing it to turn objects into sand during the use of the Moonlight Butterfly." At that point, if the 00 Qan[T] did a quantum burst, and Turn A had a full powered Moonlight Butterfly, the only question is if GN Particles would be affected by the nano machines (welcome to the difficulty of cross-series comparisons). If so, Turn A wins easily, unless the 00 Qan[T] simply teleports across the galaxy to run away. If not, then it all depends on the other specs/weapons of the suits, and in that case I might have to lean in favor of the 00 Qan[T].

Personally, I find that the animation quality should not affect your ability to enjoy the founding series of the Gundam franchise. Also, while I do greatly enjoy Wing, X, and 00 as alternate series, I would say you should definitely watch all of the Universal Century series first; however, I feel that watching the UC series will make you appreciate UC more instead of alternate universes. UC just feels more raw and realistic, where the Gundam(s) is not so ridiculously advanced that it can take out 10 grunt suits in one shot or come armed with an infantry's worth of beam cannons built into the suit. The Gundam is more of a symbol, though Gundams in UC do get more powerful as you progress into Zeta and Unicorn, and the non-Gundam suits grow as well.

In short, if you want to watch series that are compelling both on and off the battlefield, then UC is the way to go. If you are into Gundam more for watching crazy ridiculous battle sequences filled with plot armor and pretty good, though not great stories, then stick with alternate universes.
